o: Cómo Lázaro se asentó con un clérigo, y de las cosas que con él pasó.
t: How Lazarillo settled in with a cleric, and the things that happened to him there.

o: Otro día, no pareciéndome estar allí seguro, fuime a un lugar que llaman Maqueda, adonde me toparon mis pecados con un clérigo que, llegando a pedir limosna, me preguntó si sabía ayudar a misa.
t: One day, not feeling safe where I was, I went to a place called Maqueda, where my sins met me with a cleric who, coming up to ask for alms, asked me if I knew how to help at mass.

o: Yo dije que sí, como era verdad; que, aunque maltratado, mil cosas buenas me mostró el pecador del ciego, y una dellas fue ésta.
t: I said yes, as was true; for though I was ill-treated, the blind man, that sinner, showed me a thousand good things, and one of them was this.

o: Finalmente, el clérigo me recibió por suyo.
t: In the end, the cleric took me in as his own.

o: Escapé del trueno y di en el relámpago, porque era el ciego para con éste un Alejandro Magno, con ser la mesma avaricia, como he contado.
t: I escaped the thunder and fell into the lightning, because the blind man was an Alexander the Great toward this one, though it was the same greed, as I have told.

o: No digo más sino que toda la laceria del mundo estaba encerrada en éste.
t: I say only that all the wickedness in the world was shut up in him.

o: No sé si de su cosecha era, o lo había anexado con el hábito de clerecía.
t: I do not know whether it was of his own making, or whether he had added it to the habit of the clergy.

o: Él tenía un arcaz viejo y cerrado con su llave, la cual traía atada con un agujeta del paletoque, y en viniendo el bodigo de la iglesia, por su mano era luego allí lanzado, y tornada a cerrar el arca.
t: He had an old chest, locked with its key, which he carried tied with a cord from his staff, and when the church's bread came, it was thrown straight in by his own hand, and the chest locked again.

o: Y en toda la casa no había ninguna cosa de comer, como suele estar en otras: algún tocino colgado al humero, algún queso puesto en alguna tabla o en el armario, algún canastillo con algunos pedazos de pan que de la mesa sobran; que me parece a mí que aunque dello no me aprovechara, con la vista dello me consolara.
t: And there was nothing to eat anywhere in the whole house, as is usual in other houses: some bacon hanging from the chimney, some cheese set on a board or in the cupboard, some little basket with a few pieces of bread left over from the table; for it seems to me that even if it did me no good, the sight of it would comfort me.

o: Solamente había una horca de cebollas, y tras la llave en una cámara en lo alto de la casa.
t: There was only a string of onions, and behind the key, in a room high up in the house.

o: Finalmente, yo me finaba de hambre.
t: In the end, I was dying of hunger.

o: Pues, ya que conmigo tenía poca caridad, consigo usaba más.
t: Well, since he had little charity toward me, he used more with himself.

o: Cinco blancas de carne era su ordinario para comer y cenar.
t: Five whites' worth of meat was his regular allowance for dinner and supper.

o: Verdad es que partía comigo del caldo, que de la carne, ¡tan blanco el ojo!, sino un poco de pan, y ¡pluguiera a Dios que me demediara!
t: The truth is that he shared his broth with me, but of the meat — the eye so white! — only a little bread, and God grant he measured me out a portion!

o: Los sábados cómense en esta tierra cabezas de carnero, y enviábame por una que costaba tres maravedís.
t: On Saturdays they eat sheep's heads in this country, and he would send me for one that cost three maravedís.

o: Aquélla le cocía y comía los ojos y la lengua y el cogote y sesos y la carne que en las quijadas tenía, y dábame todos los huesos roídos, y dábamelos en el plato, diciendo.
t: She boiled it and ate the eyes and the tongue and the nape and the brains and the meat that was in his jaws, and gave me all the gnawed bones, and gave them to me on the plate, saying:

o: "Toma, come, triunfa, que para ti es el mundo.
t: "Here, eat, enjoy yourself, for the world is yours.

o: Mejor vida tienes que el Papa."
t: You have a better life than the Pope."

o: "¡Tal te la dé Dios!", decía yo paso entre mí.
t: "May God give you just what you deserve!" I said, as I went my way.

o: A cabo de tres semanas que estuve con él, vine a tanta flaqueza que no me podía tener en las piernas de pura hambre.
t: After three weeks of being with him, I had grown so weak that I could not keep my legs under me, purely from hunger.

o: Vime claramente ir a la sepultura, si Dios y mi saber no me remediaran.
t: I plainly saw myself on my way to the grave, unless God and my own wits could remedy me.

o: Para usar de mis mañas no tenía aparejo, por no tener en qué dalle salto; y aunque algo hubiera, no podia cegalle, como hacía al que Dios perdone, si de aquella calabazada feneció, que todavía, aunque astuto, con faltalle aquel preciado sentido no me sentía; más estotro, ninguno hay que tan aguda vista tuviese como él tenía.
t: To make use of my cunning I had no means, for I had nothing to spring from; and even if there had been something, I could not have blinded him, as I did to the one whom God forgive, if he died of that blow on the head. For still, astute as he was, that precious sense was not lacking in me; and besides, there is nobody who had so sharp a sight as he had.

o: Cuando al ofertorio estábamos, ninguna blanca en la concha caía que no era dél registrada: el un ojo tenía en la gente y el otro en mis manos.
t: When we were at the offering, not a single coin dropped into the shell that he did not have noted down: one eye he kept on the people and the other on my hands.

o: Bailábanle los ojos en el caxco como si fueran de azogue.
t: His eyes danced in the coffer as though they were made of quicksilver.

o: Cuantas blancas ofrecían tenía por cuenta; y acabado el ofrecer, luego me quitaba la concheta y la ponía sobre el altar.
t: He kept a tally of every coin that was offered; and once the offering was over, he would take the little shell away from me at once and set it on the altar.

o: No era yo señor de asirle una blanca todo el tiempo que con él veví o, por mejor decir, morí.
t: I was not master of laying hold of a single coin the whole time I lived with him, or, better said, died.

o: De la taberna nunca le traje una blanca de vino, mas aquel poco que de la ofrenda había metido en su arcaz compasaba de tal forma que le turaba toda la semana, y por ocultar su gran mezquindad decíame.
t: I never brought him so much as a coin's worth of wine from the tavern, but that little which from the offering he had put into his chest he doled out in such a way that it took him the whole week to use up, and to hide his great meanness he would tell me:

o: "Mira, mozo, los sacerdotes han de ser muy templados en su comer y beber, y por esto yo no me desmando como otros."
t: "Look, lad, priests have to be very temperate in their eating and drinking, and that is why I do not overindulge as others do."

o: Mas el lacerado mentía falsamente, porque en cofradías y mortuorios que rezamos, a costa ajena comía como lobo y bebía más que un saludador.
t: But the lacerated one lied falsely, because in the brotherhoods and the mortuaries we prayed for, at other people's expense he ate like a wolf and drank more than a beggar.

o: Y porque dije de mortuorios, Dios me perdone, que jamás fui enemigo de la naturaleza humana sino entonces, y esto era porque comíamos bien y me hartaban.
t: And because I have spoken of the dead, may God forgive me, for I was never an enemy of human nature except then, and that was because we ate well and they filled me up.

o: Deseaba y aun rogaba a Dios que cada día matase el suyo.
t: I wished, and even begged God, that He might kill his own every day.

o: Y cuando dábamos sacramento a los enfermos, especialmente la extrema unción, como manda el clérigo rezar a los que están allí, yo cierto no era el postrero de la oracion, y con todo mi corazón y buena voluntad rogaba al Señor, no que la echase a la parte que más servido fuese, como se suele decir, mas que le llevase de aqueste mundo.
t: And when we gave the sacrament to the sick, especially extreme unction, as the cleric commands us to pray for those who are there, I certainly was not the last to pray, and with all my heart and good will I begged the Lord not to cast her to the side that would serve most, as is usually said, but rather that He take her out of this world.

o: Y cuando alguno de éstos escapaba, ¡Dios me lo perdone!, que mil veces le daba al diablo, y el que se moría otras tantas bendiciones llevaba de mí dichas.
t: And when one of these escaped, may God forgive me! a thousand times I handed him over to the devil, and the one who died carried as many blessings from me as had been said.

o: Porque en todo el tiempo que allí estuve, que sería cuasi seis meses, solas veinte personas fallecieron, y éstas bien creo que las maté yo o, por mejor decir, murieron a mi recuesta; porque viendo el Señor mi rabiosa y continua muerte, pienso que holgaba de matarlos por darme a mí vida.
t: Because all the time I was there, which would be nearly six months, only twenty people died, and I firmly believe that I killed them or, better said, that they died at my request; because seeing the Lord my raging and unceasing death, I think He took pleasure in killing them in order to give me life.

o: Mas de lo que al presente padecía, remedio no hallaba, que si el día que enterrábamos yo vivía, los días que no había muerto, por quedar bien vezado de la hartura, tornando a mi cuotidiana hambre, más lo sentía.
t: But for what I suffered at present, I found no remedy, for if on the day we buried someone I still lived, on the days when no one had died, being well once more used to the fullness and returning to my daily hunger, I felt it all the more.

o: De manera que en nada hallaba descanso, salvo en la muerte, que yo también para mí como para los otros deseaba algunas veces; mas no la vía, aunque estaba siempre en mí.
t: So that in nothing did I find rest, save in death, which I also sometimes desired for myself as for the others; but I did not see the way, though it was always within me.

o: Pensé muchas veces irme de aquel mezquino amo, mas por dos cosas lo dejaba: la primera, por no me atrever a mis piernas, por temer de la flaqueza que de pura hambre me venía; y la otra, consideraba y decia.
t: I thought many times of leaving that miserable master, but for two things I stayed: the first, because I did not dare trust my legs, fearing the weakness that came on me from sheer hunger; and the other, I considered and said.

o: "Yo he tenido dos amos: el primero traíame muerto de hambre y, dejándole, topé con estotro, que me tiene ya con ella en la sepultura.
t: "I have had two masters: the first brought me dead with hunger and, leaving him, I came upon this other one, who now holds me with her in the grave."

o: Pues si deste desisto y doy en otro más bajo, ¿qué será sino fenecer?"
t: Well, if I give this up and take another, lower job, what would it be but to perish?

o: Con esto no me osaba menear, porque tenía por fe que todos los grados había de hallar más ruines; y a abajar otro punto, no sonara Lázaro ni se oyera en el mundo.
t: With this I did not dare to stir, for I held it certain that I would find every grade even more degrading; and if I stepped down another notch, neither Lázaro would be mentioned nor heard of anywhere in the world.

o: Pues, estando en tal aflición, cual plega al Señor librar della a todo fiel cristiano, y sin saber darme consejo, viéndome ir de mal en peor, un día que el cuitado ruin y lacerado de mi amo había ido fuera del lugar, llegóse acaso a mi puerta un calderero, el cual yo creo que fue ángel enviado a mí por la mano de Dios en aquel hábito.
t: Well, being in such distress as may please the Lord to lift from every faithful Christian, and unable to counsel myself, seeing myself go from bad to worse, one day, when my wretched and ragged master had gone out of the town, there chanced to come to my door a coppersmith, whom I believe was an angel sent to me by the hand of God in that guise.

o: Preguntóme si tenía algo que adobar.
t: He asked me if I had anything to mend.

o: "En mí teníades bien que hacer, y no haríades poco si me remediásedes", dije paso, que no me oyó; mas como no era tiempo de gastarlo en decir gracias, alumbrado por el Spíritu Santo, le dije.
t: "You would find plenty to do with me, and you would do little if you would relieve me," I said softly, for he did not hear me; but since it was no time to waste in giving thanks, enlightened by the Holy Spirit, I said to him.

o: "Tio, una llave de este arca he perdido, y temo mi señor me azote.
t: "Uncle, I have lost a key to this chest, and I fear my master will whip me.

o: Por vuestra vida, veáis si en ésas que traéis hay alguna que le haga, que yo os lo pagaré."
t: For your life, see if among those you carry there is one that fits it, and I will pay you."

o: Comenzó a probar el angélico caldedero una y otra de un gran sartal que dellas traía, y yo ayudalle con mis flacas oraciones.
t: The angelic coppersmith began trying one and another key from a great bunch he carried, and I helped him with my feeble prayers.

o: Cuando no me cato, veo en figura de panes, como dicen, la cara de Dios dentro del arcaz; y, abierto, díjele.
t: Before I knew it, I saw, in the shape of loaves, as they say, the face of God inside the chest; and, opening it, I said to him.

o: "Yo no tengo dineros que os dar por la llave, mas tomad de ahí el pago."
t: "I have no money to give you for the key, but take your payment from there."

o: Él tomó un bodigo de aquéllos, el que mejor le pareció, y dándome mi llave se fue muy contento, dejándome más a mí.
t: He took one of those loaves, whichever pleased him best, and handing me my key went off very happy, leaving me happier still.

o: Mas no toqué en nada por el presente, porque no fuese la falta sentida, y aun, porque me vi de tanto bien señor, parecióme que la hambre no se me osaba allegar.
t: But for the present I touched nothing, so that the loss might not be felt; and moreover, because I found myself so well provided for, it seemed to me that hunger did not dare approach me.

o: Vino el mísero de mi amo, y quiso Dios no miró en la oblada que el ángel había llevado.
t: My miserable master came, and God willed that he did not look into the offering the angel had carried off.

o: Y otro día, en saliendo de casa, abro mi paraíso panal, y tomo entre las manos y dientes un bodigo, y en dos credos le hice invisible, no se me olvidando el arca abierta; y comienzo a barrer la casa con mucha alegría, pareciéndome con aquel remedio remediar dende en adelante la triste vida.
t: And the next day, on leaving the house, I open my paradise of honeycomb, and take a loaf in my hands and teeth, and in two credos I make it disappear, not forgetting the open chest; and I begin to sweep the house with great joy, seeming to me that with that remedy I could remedy from then on my wretched life.

o: Y así estuve con ello aquel día y otro gozoso.
t: And so I stayed with it that day and the next, happy.

o: Mas no estaba en mi dicha que me durase mucho aquel descanso, porque luego al tercero día me vino la terciana derecha, y fue que veo a deshora al que me mataba de hambre sobre nuestro arcaz volviendo y revolviendo, contando y tornando a contar los panes.
t: But it was not in my luck that that rest should last me long, for on the third day the tertian fever came upon me straight, and it was that I saw at an untimely hour the one who was killing me with hunger, over our chest, turning and rummaging, counting and recounting the loaves.

o: Yo disimulaba, y en mi secreta oración y devociones y plegarias decía: "¡Sant Juan y ciégale!"
t: I kept up the appearance, and in my secret prayer and devotions and pleadings I said: "Saint John, blind him!"

o: Después que estuvo un gran rato echando la cuenta, por días y dedos contando, dijo.
t: After he had spent a long while doing the sum, counting by days and by fingers, he said.

o: "Si no tuviera a tan buen recaudo esta arca, yo dijera que me habían tomado della panes; pero de hoy más, sólo por cerrar la puerta a la sospecha, quiero tener buena cuenta con ellos: nueve quedan y un pedazo."
t: "If I did not keep this chest so carefully, I would say that loaves had been taken from it; but from today on, merely to shut the door on suspicion, I want to keep a good account of them: nine remain and a piece."

o: "¡Nuevas malas te dé Dios!", dijo yo entre mí.
t: "May God give you bad news!" said I to myself.

o: Parecióme con lo que dijo pasarme el corazón con saeta de montero, y comenzóme el estómago a escarbar de hambre, viéndose puesto en la dieta pasada.
t: It seemed to me that what he had said would happen to me had indeed happened, with the hunter's arrow in my heart, and my stomach began to gnaw at me with hunger, finding itself already set on the fare of former days.

o: Fue fuera de casa; yo, por consolarme, abro el arca, y como vi el pan, comencélo de adorar, no osando recebillo.
t: He was out of the house; I, to console myself, open the chest, and as I saw the bread I began to adore it, not daring to take it.

o: Contélos, si a dicha el lacerado se errara, y hallé su cuenta más verdadera que yo quisiera.
t: I told him, in case the wretched man had been mistaken, and I found his account truer than I could have wished.

o: Lo más que yo pude hacer fue dar en ellos mil besos y, lo más delicado que yo pude, del partido partí un poco al pelo que él estaba; y con aquél pasé aquel día, no tan alegre como el pasado.
t: The most I could do was to give them a thousand kisses and, as delicately as I could, I broke off a little of the piece he was at, right at the edge; and with that I got through that day, not as cheerful as the one before.

o: Mas como la hambre creciese, mayormente que tenía el estómago hecho a más pan aquellos dos o tres días ya dichos, moría mala muerte; tanto, que otra cosa no hacía en viéndome solo sino abrir y cerrar el arca y contemplar en aquella cara de Dios, que ansí dicen los niños.
t: But as the hunger grew, mainly because my stomach had been made used to more bread those two or three days already spoken of, I was dying a bad death; so much so, that all I did when I saw myself alone was open and close the chest and gaze upon that face of God, which is what the children call it.

o: Mas el mesmo Dios, que socorre a los afligidos, viéndome en tal estrecho, trujo a mi memoria un pequeño remedio; que, considerando entre mí, dije.
t: But the same God, who succors the afflicted, seeing me in such a strait, brought to my mind a small remedy; for, thinking it over, I said.

o: "Este arquetón es viejo y grande y roto por algunas partes, aunque pequeños agujeros.
t: "This chest is old and big and broken in some places, though with small holes.

o: Puédese pensar que ratones, entrando en él, hacen daño a este pan.
t: One may think that mice, getting into it, do damage to this bread.

o: Sacarlo entero no es cosa conveniente, porque verá la falta el que en tanta me hace vivir.
t: To take it out whole is not a fitting thing, because the one who keeps me in such straits will see the lack.

o: Esto bien se sufre."
t: This can well be borne."

o: Y comienzo a desmigajar el pan sobre unos no muy costosos manteles que allí estaban; y tomo uno y dejo otro, de manera que en cada cual de tres o cuatro desmigajé su poco; después, como quien toma gragea, lo comí, y algo me consolé.
t: And I begin to crumble the bread over some not very costly tablecloths that were there; and I take one and leave another, so that in each of three or four I crumbled a little; then, like one who takes a sweetmeat, I ate it, and I was somewhat consoled.

o: Mas él, como viniese a comer y abriese el arca, vio el mal pesar, y sin dubda creyó ser ratones los que el daño habían hecho, porque estaba muy al propio contrahecho de como ellos lo suelen hacer.
t: But he, as he came to eat and opened the chest, saw the damage, and without doubt believed that mice had done the damage, because it was very much in keeping with how they usually do it.

o: Miró todo el arcaz de un cabo a otro y viole ciertos agujeros por do sospechaba habían entrado.
t: He looked over the whole chest from end to end and saw certain holes where he suspected they had got in.

o: Llamóme, diciendo.
t: He called me, saying.

o: "¡Lázaro! ¡Mira, mira qué persecución ha venido aquesta noche por nuestro pan!"
t: "Lazarillo! Look, look what a pest has come to our bread tonight!"

o: Yo híceme muy maravillado, preguntándole qué sería.
t: I made myself very much astonished, asking him what it might be.

o: -dijo él-. Ratones, que no dejan cosa a vida."
t: -said he-. Mice, which leave nothing alive."

o: Pusímonos a comer, y quiso Dios que aun en esto me fue bien, que me cupo más pan que la laceria que me solía dar, porque rayó con un cuchillo todo lo que pensó ser ratonado, diciendo.
t: We set to eating, and God willed that even in this I should fare well, for there fell to me more bread than the stinginess usually gave me, because he scraped with a knife everything he thought had been gnawed by mice, saying.

o: "Cómete eso, que el ratón cosa limpia es."
t: "Eat that, for a mouse is clean stuff."

o: Y así aquel día, añadiendo la ración del trabajo de mis manos, o de mis uñas, por mejor decir, acabamos de comer, aunque yo nunca empezaba.
t: And so that day, adding the ration of the work of my hands, or of my nails, rather, we finished eating, though I never used to begin.

o: Y luego me vino otro sobresalto, que fue verle andar solícito, quitando clavos de las paredes y buscando tablillas, con las cuales clavó y cerró todos los agujeros de la vieja arca.
t: And then another fright came to me, which was seeing him busily pulling nails out of the walls and hunting for thin boards, with which he nailed up and closed every hole in the old chest.

o: -dije yo entonces-, ¡a cuánta miseria y fortuna y desastres estamos puestos los nacidos, y cuán poco turan los placeres de esta nuestra trabajosa vida!
t: "-said I then-, into how much misery and fortune and disaster are we born, and how little do the pleasures of this our laborious life last!

o: Así lamentaba yo, en tanto que mi solícito carpintero con muchos clavos y tablillas dio fin a sus obras, diciendo: "Agora, donos traidores ratones, conviéneos mudar propósito, que en esta casa mala medra tenéis."
t: Thus I lamented, while my diligent carpenter, with many nails and boards, brought his work to an end, saying: "Now, you traitorous mice, it behoves us to change our tune, for in this bad house you have your breeding ground."

o: De que salió de su casa, voy a ver la obra y hallé que no dejó en la triste y vieja arca agujero ni aun por dónde le pudiese entrar un moxquito.
t: When he came out of his house, I went to see the work and found that he had left in the sad old chest no hole, not even one through which a mosquito might enter.

o: Abro con mi desaprovechada llave, sin esperanza de sacar provecho, y vi los dos o tres panes comenzados, los que mi amo creyó ser ratonados, y dellos todavía saqué alguna laceria, tocándolos muy ligeramente, a uso de esgremidor diestro.
t: I open it with my ill-used key, with no hope of getting any profit, and saw the two or three loaves already cut into, which my master thought had been gnawed by mice, and from them I still took some morsels, touching them very lightly, as a skilled fencer does.

o: Como la necesidad sea tan gran maestra, viéndome con tanta, siempre, noche y día, estaba pensando la manera que ternía en sustentar el vivir; y pienso, para hallar estos negros remedios, que me era luz la hambre, pues dicen que el ingenio con ella se avisa y al contrario con la hartura, y así era por cierto en mí.
t: Since necessity is such a great teacher, seeing myself in such need, always, night and day, I was turning over the way I should have to sustain life; and I think, to find these black remedies, that hunger was my light, for they say that wit grows sharp with it and dull with surfeit, and so it truly was with me.

o: Pues estando una noche desvelado en este pensamiento, pensando como me podría valer y aprovecharme del arcaz, sentí que mi amo dormía, porque lo mostraba con roncar y en unos resoplidos grandes que daba cuando estaba durmiendo.
t: Now, one night, lying awake with this thought, pondering how I might make use of the chest, I felt that my master was asleep, because he showed it by snoring and by the great snorts he gave when he was sleeping.

o: Levantéme muy quedito y, habiendo en el día pensado lo que había de hacer y dejado un cuchillo viejo que por allí andaba en parte do le hallase, voyme al triste arcaz, y por do había mirado tener menos defensa le acometí con el cuchillo, que a manera de barreno dél usé.
t: I got up very quietly and, having thought out during the day what I was to do and left an old knife that lay about where I found it, I went to the sad chest, and at the point where I had seen it to be least defended I set at it with the knife, which I used as a drill.

o: Y como la antiquísima arca, por ser de tantos años, la hallase sin fuerza y corazón, antes muy blanda y carcomida, luego se me rindió, y consintió en su costado por mi remedio un buen agujero.
t: And since the very ancient chest, being so many years old, was without strength and heart, before very soft and rotten, it soon yielded to me, and granted me in its side, for my remedy, a good hole.

o: Esto hecho, abro muy paso la llagada arca y, al tiento, del pan que hallé partido hice según deyuso está escrito.
t: This done, I opened the wounded chest very slowly and, by feel, from the bread I found split I did as is written below.

o: Y con aquello algún tanto consolado, tornando a cerrar, me volví a mis pajas, en las cuales reposé y dormí un poco, lo cual yo hacía mal, y echábalo al no comer; y ansí sería, porque cierto en aquel tiempo no me debían de quitar el sueño los cuidados del rey de Francia.
t: And with that somewhat consoled, turning to close it again, I went back to my straw, where I rested and slept a little, which I did ill, and blamed it on not eating; and so it was, for certainly at that time the cares of the King of France were not going to rob me of my sleep.

o: Otro día fue por el señor mi amo visto el daño así del pan como del agujero que yo había hecho, y comenzó a dar a los diablos los ratones y decir.
t: Another day my master, the lord, saw the damage both to the bread and to the hole I had made, and began to give the mice to the devil and to say:

o: "¿Qué diremos a esto?
t: "What shall we say to this?

o: ¡Nunca haber sentido ratones en esta casa sino agora!"
t: "Never have I had mice in this house until now!"

o: Y sin dubda debía de decir verdad; porque si casa había de haber en el reino justamente de ellos privilegiada, aquélla de razón había de ser, porque no suelen morar donde no hay qué comer.
t: And without doubt he spoke the truth; because if there were a house in the kingdom privileged for them, it would rightly be this one, for they do not usually dwell where there is nothing to eat.

o: Torna a buscar clavos por la casa y por las paredes y tablillas a atapárselos.
t: He goes back to look for nails around the house and on the walls, and thin boards to nail over them.

o: Venida la noche y su reposo, luego era yo puesto en pie con mi aparejo, y cuantos él tapaba de día, destapaba yo de noche.
t: Night and its rest having come, I was at once on my feet with my gear, and as many holes as he covered by day, I uncovered by night.

o: En tal manera fue, y tal priesa nos dimos, que sin dubda por esto se debió decir: "Donde una puerta se cierra, otra se abre."
t: In such manner it was, and such haste we gave ourselves, that without doubt it was because of this that it was said: "Where one door closes, another opens."

o: Finalmente, parecíamos tener a destajo la tela de Penélope, pues cuanto él tejía de día, rompía yo de noche; ca en pocos días y noches pusimos la pobre despensa de tal forma, que quien quisiera propiamente della hablar, más corazas viejas de otro tiempo que no arcaz la llamara, según la clavazón y tachuelas sobre sí tenía.
t: Finally, we seemed to have Penelope's web by the piece, for as much as he wove by day I broke by night; and in a few days and nights we put the poor larder into such a state, that anyone who wanted to speak properly of it would have called it a heap of old corsets from another age rather than a chest, given the nails and tacks it had upon it.

o: De que vio no le aprovechar nada su remedio, dijo.
t: When he saw that his remedy availed him nothing, he said.

o: "Este arcaz está tan maltratado y es de madera tan vieja y flaca, que no habrá ratón a quien se defienda; y va ya tal que, si andamos más con él, nos dejará sin guarda; y aun lo peor, que aunque hace poca, todavía hará falta faltando, y me pondrá en costa de tres o cuatro reales.
t: "This chest is so battered and made of such old, thin wood that no mouse will be able to defend itself against it; and it is already in such a state that if we keep on with it, it will leave us without a guard; and worst of all, even though it makes little, it will still be needed when it goes missing, and will put me in the hole for three or four reales."

o: El mejor remedio que hallo, pues el de hasta aquí no aprovecha, armaré por de dentro a estos ratopes malditos."
t: The best remedy I can find, since the one used until now doesn't work, is to arm these accursed rats from the inside."

o: Luego buscó prestada una ratonera, y con cortezas de queso que a los vecinos pedía, contino el gato estaba armado dentro del arca, lo cual era para mí singular auxilio; porque, puesto caso que yo no había menester muchas salsas para comer, todavía me holgaba con las cortezas del queso que de la ratonera sacaba, y sin esto no perdonaba el ratonar del bodigo.
t: Then he borrowed a mousetrap, and with cheese rinds that he begged from the neighbors, he had the cat armed inside the chest, which was a singular help for me; because, supposing I did not need many sauces to eat, I still took pleasure in the cheese rinds I pulled from the mousetrap, and without these he would not forgive the rat-holed loaf.

o: Como hallase el pan ratonado y el queso comido y no cayese el ratón que lo comía, dábase al diablo, preguntaba a los vecinos qué podría ser comer el queso y sacarlo de la ratonera, y no caer ni quedar dentro el ratón, y hallar caída la trampilla del gato.
t: When he found the bread rat-eaten and the cheese eaten and the mouse that ate it did not fall, he cursed, and asked the neighbors what it could be that ate the cheese and took it out of the mousetrap, and neither fell nor stayed inside the mouse, and found the cat's trapdoor down.

o: Acordaron los vecinos no ser el ratón el que este daño hacía, porque no fuera menos de haber caído alguna vez. Díjole un vecino.
t: The neighbors agreed that it was not the mouse that was doing this damage, because it would be no less than having fallen at some point. A neighbor told him.

o: "En vuestra casa yo me acuerdo que solía andar una culebra, y ésta debe ser sin dubda.
t: "In your house I remember a snake used to wander about, and this must be it beyond a doubt.

o: Y lleva razón que, como es larga, tiene lugar de tomar el cebo; y aunque la coja la trampilla encima, como no entre toda dentro, tórnase a salir."
t: And he is right, because, since it is long, it has room to take the bait; and even if the trapdoor catches it on top, since it does not get entirely inside, it turns and comes out again."

o: Cuadró a todos lo que aquél dijo, y alteró mucho a mi amo; y dende en adelante no dormía tan a sueño suelto, que cualquier gusano de la madera que de noche sonase, pensaba ser la culebra que le roía el arca.
t: What that man said seemed right to everyone, and it disturbed my master greatly; and from then on he did not sleep so soundly that any worm in the wood that made a noise at night, he thought was the snake gnawing his chest.

o: Luego era puesto en pie, y con un garrote que a la cabacera, desde que aquello le dijeron, ponía, daba en la pecadora del arca grandes garrotazos, pensando espantar la culebra.
t: Then he would get up on his feet, and with a cudgel that he set at the head of the bed, ever since they had told him that, he would deal the chest's sinner great blows, thinking to scare off the snake.

o: A los vecinos despertaba con el estruendo que hacía, y a mí no me dejaba dormir. êbase a mis pajas y trastornábalas, y a mí con ellas, pensando que se iba para mí y se envolvía en mis pajas o en mi sayo, porque le decían que de noche acaecía a estos animales, buscando calor, irse a las cunas donde están criaturas y aun mordellas y hacerles peligrar.
t: He woke the neighbors with the noise he made, and would not let me sleep. He turned to my straw and upset it, and me along with it, thinking it was coming for me and wrapping itself in my straw or in my cloak, because they told him that these animals come at night seeking warmth, going to the cradles where there are children and even puppies, and putting them in danger.

o: Yo las más veces hacía del dormido, y en las mañas decíame él.
t: Most of the time I played the sleeper, and he told me his tricks.

o: "Esta noche, mozo, ¿no sentiste nada?
t: "Tonight, lad, didn't you feel anything?"

o: Pues tras la culebra anduve, y aun pienso se ha de ir para ti a la cama, que son muy frías y buscan calor."
t: Well, I went after the snake, and I still think it will come to you in bed, since they are very cold and seek warmth."

o: "Plega a Dios que no me muerda -decía yo-, que harto miedo le tengo."
t: "God please it doesn't bite me," said I, "for I am plenty afraid of it."

o: De esta manera andaba tan elevado y levantado del sueño, que, mi fe, la culebra (o culebro, por mejor decir) no osaba roer de noche ni levantarse al arca; mas de día, mientra estaba en la iglesia o por el lugar, hacía mis saltos: los cuales daños viendo él y el poco remedio que les podía poner, andaba de noche, como digo, hecho trasgo.
t: In this way he went about so elevated and lifted out of sleep that, upon my honor, the snake (or snake, better said) did not dare gnaw at night nor rise to the chest; but by day, while he was at church or about the place, he took his leaps: which damages seeing, and the little remedy he could give them, he went about at night, as I say, made a coward.

o: Yo hube miedo que con aquellas diligencias no me topase con la llave que debajo de las pajas tenía, y parecióme lo más seguro metella de noche en la boca.
t: I feared that with those goings-on he might come upon the key I had under the straw, and it seemed to me the safest thing to put it in my mouth at night.

o: Porque ya, desde que viví con el ciego, la tenía tan hecha bolsa que me acaeció tener en ella doce o quince maravedís, todo en medias blancas, sin que me estorbasen el comer; porque de otra manera no era señor de una blanca que el maldito ciego no cayese con ella, no dejando costura ni remiendo que no me buscaba muy a menudo.
t: Because already, since I lived with the blind man, I had it so well worn as a purse that it happened to me to have in it twelve or fifteen maravedís, all in silver halves, without their troubling my eating; because otherwise he was not master of a single blanca that the accursed blind man did not fall with, leaving no seam or patch that he did not very often search.

o: Pues ansí, como digo, metía cada noche la llave en la boca, y dormía sin recelo que el brujo de mi amo cayese con ella; mas cuando la desdicha ha de venir, por demás es diligencia.
t: Well, thus, as I say, every night I put the key in my mouth, and slept without fear that my master's wizard would fall with it; but when misfortune is coming, diligence is in vain.

o: Levantóse muy paso con su garrote en la mano, y al tiento y sonido de la culebra se llegó a mí con mucha quietud, por no ser sentido de la culebra; y como cerca se vio, pensó que allí en las pajas do yo estaba echado, al calor mío se había venido.
t: He rose very quietly with his cudgel in his hand, and by the feel and sound of the snake he came up to me with great quietness, so as not to be heard by the snake; and when he saw himself close, he thought that there in the straw where I lay, it had come for my warmth.

o: Levantando bien el palo, pensando tenerla debajo y darle tal garrotazo que la matase, con toda su fuerza me descargó en la cabeza un tan gran golpe, que sin ningún sentido y muy mal descalabrado me dejó.
t: Raising the stick well, thinking to have her underneath and give her such a blow as to kill her, he unloaded on my head with all his strength a blow so great that he left me without a single sense and badly cracked in the head.

o: Como sintió que me había dado, según yo debía hacer gran sentimiento con el fiero golpe, contaba él que se había llegado a mí y dándome grandes voces, llamándome, procuró recordarme.
t: When he felt he had given me such a blow that, as I think, he should have felt great remorse for the fierce stroke, he told me that he had come up to me and, raising his voice and calling to me, had tried to bring me to my senses.

o: Mas como me tocase con las manos, tentó la mucha sangre que se me iba, y conoció el daño que me había hecho, y con mucha priesa fue a buscar lumbre.
t: But when he touched me with his hands, he tried the plentiful blood that was draining from me, and knew the harm he had done me, and in great haste went to look for fire.

o: Y llegando con ella, hallóme quejando, todavía con mi llave en la boca, que nunca la desamparé, la mitad fuera, bien de aquella manera que debía estar al tiempo que silbaba con ella.
t: And coming back with it, he found me complaining, still with my key in my mouth — I never let it go — half of it out, just as it had to be at the time I blew it.

o: Espantado el matador de culebras qué podría ser aquella llave, miróla, sacándomela del todo de la boca, y vio lo que era, porque en las guardas nada de la suya diferenciaba.
t: The snake-killer, frightened at what that key might be, looked at it, pulling it all out of my mouth, and saw what it was, because in the wards it differed in no way from his own.

o: Fue luego a proballa, y con ella probó el maleficio.
t: He then went to try it, and with it he tried the charm.

o: Debió de decir el cruel cazador: "El ratón y culebra que me daban guerra y me comían mi hacienda he hallado."
t: The cruel hunter must have said: "The mouse and the snake that were making war on me and eating up my estate I have found."

o: De lo que sucedió en aquellos tres días siguientes ninguna fe daré, porque los tuve en el vientre de la ballena; mas de cómo esto que he contado oí, después que en mí torné, decir a mi amo, el cual a cuantos allí venían lo contaba por extenso.
t: Of what happened in those three following days I will give no account, for I spent them in the whale's belly; but of what I have told, I heard, after I came back to myself, my master say, and he recounted it at length to all who came there.

o: A cabo de tres días yo torné en mi sentido y vine echado en mis pajas, la cabeza toda emplastada y llena de aceites y ungüentos y, espantado, dije: "¿Qué es esto?"
t: At the end of three days I came back to my senses and found myself lying on my straw, my head all plastered and covered with oils and ointments, and, frightened, I said: "What is this?"

o: Respondióme el cruel sacerdote.
t: The cruel priest answered me.

o: "A fe, que los ratones y culebras que me destruían ya los he cazado."
t: "Indeed, the mice and the snakes that were destroying me I have already hunted down."

o: Y miré por mí, y vime tan maltratado que luego sospeché mi mal.
t: And I looked at myself and saw myself so ill-treated that I soon suspected my misfortune.

o: A esta hora entró una vieja que ensalmaba, y los vecinos, y comiénzanme a quitar trapos de la cabeza y curar el garrotazo.
t: At that hour there came in an old woman who knew her herbs, and the neighbors, and they began to take the cloths off my head and treat the blow.

o: Y como me hallaron vuelto en mi sentido, holgáronse mucho y dijeron.
t: And when they found me back in my senses, they rejoiced greatly and said:

o: "Pues ha tornado en su acuerdo, placerá a Dios no será nada."
t: "Well, he has come to his senses; please God it will be nothing."

o: Ahí tornaron de nuevo a contar mis cuitas y a reírlas, y yo, pecador, a llorarlas.
t: Thereupon they began again to tell my troubles and laugh at them, and I, sinner, to weep over them.

o: Con todo esto, diéronme de comer, que estaba transido de hambre, y apenas me pudieron remediar.
t: With all this, they gave me food, for I was worn out with hunger, and they could scarcely relieve me.

o: Y ansí, de poco en poco, a los quince días me levanté y estuve sin peligro, mas no sin hambre, y medio sano.
t: And so, little by little, on the fifteenth day I got up and was out of danger, though not without hunger, and half healed.

o: Luego otro día que fui levantado, el señor mi amo me tomó por la mano y sacóme la puerta fuera y, puesto en la calle, díjome.
t: Then, another day when I had risen, my lord my master took me by the hand and led me out the door, and, set me in the street, said to me:

o: Lázaro, de hoy más eres tuyo y no mío.
t: Lazarillo, from this day forward you are yours and not mine.

o: Busca amo y vete con Dios, que yo no quiero en mi compañía tan diligente servidor.
t: Find a master and go with God, for I do not want in my company so diligent a servant.

o: No es posible sino que hayas sido mozo de ciego."
t: There's no way you could have been anything but a blind man's boy.

o: Y santiguándose de mí como si yo estuviera endemoniado, tórnase a meter en casa y cierra su puerta.
t: And crossing himself against me, as if I were possessed, he goes back into the house and shuts the door.
